scope: All test files with 4+ classification markers (contract, integration, e2e, real_artifact, adversarial, substrate, sabotage, flaky, slow, network, provider, destructive, migration, quarantine, smoke)

summary.methodology: Markers were audited against test content: adversarial requires injection/corruption/escape intent; substrate requires storage/cache/infrastructure checks; real_artifact requires real file artifact consumption; integration requires cross-component exercise

findings.notes: Has module-level pytestmark=[pytest.mark.migration] which flags the entire file. Individual tests then stack additional markers. The module-level migration marker means every test carries migration regardless of content.

findings.notes: This file uses module-level pytestmark assigning ALL FIVE markers to EVERY test. This is the most severe overlabeling case. 18 test methods inherit 5 markers regardless of content. Tests like test_loads_target_schema (simple isinstance check) carry adversarial and substrate markers. The file should drop module-level pytestmark and assign per-test markers.

recommendations: Module-level pytestmark with 4+ classification markers should be replaced by per-test/per-class markers
adversarial marker should require: injection/corruption/malformed input crafting (not just checking exit codes or string presence)
substrate marker should require: storage layer, cache, infrastructure, or filesystem edge cases (not just side-effect isolation)
real_artifact marker should require: actual consumption of repo file artifacts (not just schema structure checks)
Consider adding a CI lint rule (similar to pytest-check-marks) to warn when a test carries more than 3 classification markers
